title: Risk assessment — issue #3364 skill-slim: three independent slices B (monitoring tooling), C (supervision cap-wall hardening), D (gated skill deletion)
summary: Three file-disjoint slices with three distinct risk profiles, grounded live against the tree (2026-07-06). PR B is additive/LOW — its only real hazard is emitting slice.closed inside the scheduler lock (deadlock) and forgetting the /status/wait allowlist entry (silent drop). PR C is the heaviest slice (MEDIUM-HIGH) AND has been sent back for re-scope by cq-2 (resolved opt-3, 'pause & re-plan'): implement discovered the plan's central premise is FALSE — throttle error TEXT (429/'rate limit'/'overloaded') is NOT observable at the recording/streak site because only the agent's process EXIT CODE propagates to the orchestrator (egg_agent/__main__.py:143; kubernetes_spawner exit_detail is just 'exit_code=N', _models.py:131). AC-C1 ('classify as transient rate-limit, NOT abnormal, NOT trip the fail-streak halt') is therefore UNACHIEVABLE at the 3 contracted files; the only faithful mechanism is a distinct exit code (EX_RATE_LIMITED) mirroring EX_AUTH_FATAL, plumbed egg_agent/auth_errors.py → egg_agent/__main__.py → kubernetes_spawner/_models.py(outcome_for) → event_loop/_loop.py(_observe_jobs) → event_loop/_supervisor.py(a new record_rate_limited, paced/no-streak-halt) — ~7 files. Compounding it, the #3447 decomposition MOVED JobSupervisor out of concurrent_executor.py into orchestrator/event_loop/ AFTER the plan's anchors were written, so every PR C anchor (JobSupervisor integration, streak site) must be re-grounded. The remaining PR C hazards stand: over-broad classification masking real failures, a loop guard that is now the ONLY structural stop (cq-1 removed the wall-clock ceiling), landed-slice preservation. PR D is MEDIUM (gated deletion): the coverage-map gate must be real verification (D1 blocks D2/D3), over-deletion must not take out the render-on-alert AskUserQuestion flows, and the host agent-* vocab has NO deterministic emitter today (only a dedup map + the Haiku classifier LLM path), so 'parity' rests partly on a probabilistic path and any unmapped block is a HITL, not a silent delete.
grounded_against_tree: 2026-07-06. Verified live: auth_errors.py docstring :24-29 + comment :45-47 (429/'rate limit'/'overloaded' intentionally absent from _AUTH_FATAL_PATTERNS; a weekly/usage cap still matches on its own wording even over a 429); EX_AUTH_FATAL=77 exit code emitted at egg_agent/__main__.py:143, and per its comment 'only the CLI's process exit code, which is what propagates to k8s, carries the auth-fatal signal' → error TEXT does NOT reach the orchestrator recording layer; kubernetes_spawner/_models.py outcome_for(:44) maps to JOB_OUTCOME_{RUNNING,SUCCESS,ABNORMAL,FATAL}, exit_detail_for(:102) returns 'exit_code=N' (:131) — no text; event_loop/_loop.py _observe_jobs(:54) calls supervisor.record_fatal(:101)/record_abort(:119); JobSupervisor now at orchestrator/event_loop/__init__.py:368 with record_success/record_fatal/record_abnormal/record_legitimate_outcome in event_loop/_supervisor.py (#3447 relocation, POST-plan); all-producers exhaustion notifier is _handle_arms_exhausted at concurrent_executor.py:1076 (wired :559) — the plan's ':988' streak anchor is STALE; supervision_policy.py SUPERVISION_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS=30; slice_scheduler.py _hitl_escalator Callable seam injected at __init__ (:159/180) and invoked OUTSIDE the lock (:352-357), record_complete (:361)/record_failure (:371) emit NO event today; cq-1 resolved human opt-3 (unbounded paced retry + threshold OVERSEER_ALERT, NO hard ceiling); cq-2 resolved human opt-3 (pause PR C, re-plan/re-scope to reconcile file set with #3447 relocation).

risks.risk: slice.closed emitter invoked while the SliceScheduler lock is held → re-entrancy / deadlock that hangs the scheduler and stalls the whole pipeline.
risks.mitigation: Mirror the existing _hitl_escalator seam exactly: inject the emitter Callable at __init__ (default None, stored), and invoke it OUTSIDE the lock (as the escalator fires at :352-357), never inside record_complete/record_failure's `with self._lock:` block. Reviewer criterion: emitter call site is post-lock-release in BOTH record_complete and record_failure.
risks.review_gate: Confirm emitter fires outside the lock in both sites; a test that a completion and a failure each emit exactly one event without deadlock.

risks.risk: 'slice.closed' omitted from _STATUS_WAIT_EVENT_TYPES (routes/pipelines/__init__.py:405) → the event is dropped by the /status/wait allowlist filter (_routes_status.py:349) before reaching wait-status consumers; the feature ships dead-on-arrival.
risks.mitigation: Add 'slice.closed' to the allowlist in the same slice; test asserts the emitted event survives the /status/wait filter.
risks.review_gate: Allowlist entry present + a test that slice.closed passes /status/wait.

risks.risk: --exclude-types / --quiet filtering regresses the default (unfiltered) output path or the existing --since/--inner-timeout/--max-iterations behavior of the launcher the skill's Monitor loop depends on.
risks.mitigation: Apply filtering only at the two json.dumps print sites (:249/:271); default (no flags) output byte-identical. Regression test: default output unchanged; --since/--inner-timeout/--max-iterations still behave.
risks.review_gate: Regression test for un-flagged default output.

risks.risk: Adding new imports/deps to the pure-stdlib self-contained launcher breaks its portability contract.
risks.mitigation: Client-side set-membership filtering with stdlib only; no new imports.
risks.review_gate: grep the diff for new import lines in skills/sdlc/bin/wait-status.

risks.risk: Over-broad transient rate-limit classification captures genuine abnormal / deterministic code failures, so a real bug is retried forever under 'cap wall' cover and never surfaces. This is the central hazard of the slice.
risks.mitigation: Key the new class STRICTLY off the conjunction: (a) the transient-rate-limit EXIT CODE (a new EX_RATE_LIMITED, decided at the agent CLI where the error text IS available — see RC8; NOT re-derived from text at the orchestrator, which never sees it) AND (b) the all-producers signature at the arms-exhausted notifier (_handle_arms_exhausted, concurrent_executor.py:1076 — NOT the stale :988). A single producer, or any non-rate-limited exit code, stays on the existing abnormal path. Invariance guard (AC-C6): EX_AUTH_FATAL and ordinary abnormal behave UNCHANGED.
risks.review_gate: Tests: rate-limited exit-code streak → transient rate-limit (not abnormal, no fail-streak halt); single-producer / non-throttling exit → still abnormal; EX_AUTH_FATAL (incl. matched weekly cap) → still fatal, NOT reclassified as transient retry.

risks.risk: Deterministic-loop guard fails to detect identical reproduction → infinite retry loop. Because cq-1 removed the wall-clock ceiling, this guard is now the ONLY structural stop for a failure that merely LOOKS transient but is actually deterministic.
risks.mitigation: Capture a stable failure fingerprint = failure signature + phase/slice progression. If a restart reproduces the IDENTICAL fingerprint at the SAME point, stop and escalate (deterministic) instead of looping. This slice warrants the heaviest test coverage in the pipeline.
risks.review_gate: Test: identical fingerprint across a restart → escalates (does not loop).

risks.risk: Loop-guard FALSE POSITIVE — an advancing-state retry is mistaken for an identical reproduction → premature escalate/halt, defeating the intended auto-recovery across a multi-hour cap window.
risks.mitigation: Fingerprint must include phase/slice progression so 'the restart advanced state' → continue; only same-signature-AND-same-point → escalate.
risks.review_gate: Test: restart that advances state → continues (does NOT escalate).

risks.risk: The restart_phase-equivalent resets completed slice runtimes → discards landed slice work (AC-C3 violation), forcing already-consensus-confirmed slices to re-run.
risks.mitigation: Re-arm only the in-flight / failed frontier; never reset SchedulerSliceState.COMPLETE runtimes or their completed_at.
risks.review_gate: Test: landed (COMPLETE) slices are preserved across a paced-retry restart.

risks.risk: Conflating the deterministic-loop-guard escalation with a wall-clock time-ceiling halt → violates the binding cq-1 resolution (operator explicitly chose opt-3: NO hard ceiling). The two triggers are orthogonal.
risks.mitigation: No hard wall-clock halt anywhere in the new path. The only escalations are (a) threshold OVERSEER_ALERT (visibility, not halt) and (b) loop-guard on identical reproduction. Keep them independent.
risks.review_gate: Reviewer verifies no time-elapsed halt is introduced; threshold path emits an alert and CONTINUES retrying.

risks.risk: Threshold OVERSEER_ALERT never fires (operator blind during a multi-day cap) or fires repeatedly (alert fatigue / dedup missing).
risks.mitigation: Emit once the cumulative wait crosses the threshold; dedup so a persistent cap does not re-alert every retry.
risks.review_gate: Test: threshold OVERSEER_ALERT fires once at the crossing, not per-retry.

risks.risk: Paced-retry window state shared across producers in JobSupervisor introduces a thread-safety race at the streak-tracking site (now event_loop/_supervisor.py, per #3447 — NOT the stale concurrent_executor.py:988), corrupting the classification or the retry cadence.
risks.mitigation: Guard the shared window/streak state under the existing supervisor synchronization in event_loop/_supervisor.py; do not introduce lock-free mutation of the streak counter.
risks.review_gate: Reviewer confirms shared retry-window state mutation is synchronized in the relocated JobSupervisor (event_loop/_supervisor.py).

risks.risk: AC-C1 ('classify as transient rate-limit, NOT abnormal, does NOT trip the fail-streak halt') is UNACHIEVABLE at the 3 contracted files (supervision_policy.py, auth_errors.py, concurrent_executor.py). Implement (cq-2) proved the orchestrator recording layer never sees the agent's error TEXT — only the process EXIT CODE propagates (egg_agent/__main__.py:143 comment; kubernetes_spawner exit_detail is 'exit_code=N', _models.py:131). Any classification that tries to read 429/'rate limit'/'overloaded' wording at the streak/exhaustion site is reading text that is not there → the throttle streak silently records as abnormal and trips the per-key streak>=10 halt anyway, defeating the whole slice. Operator resolved cq-2 opt-3 (pause & re-scope).
risks.mitigation: The re-scoped plan MUST adopt the exit-code mechanism mirroring EX_AUTH_FATAL: classify at the agent CLI where error text is live (add is_transient_rate_limit_error + EX_RATE_LIMITED to auth_errors.py; return it at __main__.py:143), map it through kubernetes_spawner outcome_for (new JOB_OUTCOME_RATE_LIMITED), branch it in event_loop/_loop.py:_observe_jobs, and intercept it at the per-arm RECORDING layer with a new event_loop/_supervisor.py:record_rate_limited that pace-retries WITHOUT incrementing the fail-streak. This expands PR C from 3 to ~7 files. If the re-plan instead chooses to stay at 3 files (cq-2 opt-2), it must EXPLICITLY document that AC-C1's 'not abnormal / no fail-streak halt' is only PARTIALLY met (per-key streak still trips, per-producer AGENT_FAILED HITLs still fire) — the operator did NOT choose opt-2, so a silent 3-file scope that claims full AC-C1 is a NACK.
risks.review_gate: Re-scoped PR C plan names the exit-code chain (auth_errors → __main__ → kubernetes_spawner → event_loop/_loop → event_loop/_supervisor) OR explicitly documents the opt-2 partial-AC-C1 deviation; reviewer confirms the classification is decided where the error text is available, not re-derived at a text-blind site.

risks.slice: PR C (slice 2) — #3447 relocation seam + expanded blast radius
risks.risk: The faithful mechanism (RC8) now spans ~7 files across THREE containers/packages (shared/egg_agent, orchestrator/kubernetes_spawner, orchestrator/event_loop, orchestrator/concurrent_executor) instead of the contracted 3, and JobSupervisor relocated to orchestrator/event_loop/ (#3447) after the plan anchors were written. A wider surface = larger regression blast radius on the LIVE supervision path (a bug here can wedge or prematurely halt EVERY pipeline, not just #3364), and stale anchors (concurrent_executor.py:988; 'JobSupervisor in concurrent_executor.py') will misdirect the coder.
risks.mitigation: Re-ground every PR C anchor to post-#3447 reality (JobSupervisor: event_loop/__init__.py:368; recording layer: event_loop/_supervisor.py record_*; all-producers signal: concurrent_executor.py:1076 _handle_arms_exhausted). Update the contract task file-set for slice-2 to the reconciled ~7-file list. Keep the exit-code path additive (new EX_RATE_LIMITED / JOB_OUTCOME_RATE_LIMITED / record_rate_limited) so EX_AUTH_FATAL and abnormal remain byte-for-byte on their existing branches (AC-C6). Heaviest test coverage in the pipeline: classification, pacing/window, landed-slice preservation, loop-guard both directions, and an explicit AC-C6 invariance regression across the NEW plumbing.
risks.review_gate: task_planner's slice-2 file-set matches the reconciled scope and post-#3447 anchors; reviewer confirms no stale concurrent_executor.py:988 / 'JobSupervisor in concurrent_executor' anchors survive; AC-C6 invariance test exercises the new exit-code branches.

risks.risk: The coverage-map gate is skipped or rubber-stamped and a host detector is deleted with NO overseer equivalent → that detection goes silently dark for every pipeline, not just attended /sdlc sessions.
risks.mitigation: D1 (coverage-map) MUST be a task-level blocker on D2 (SKILL.md deletion) and D3 (flag removal) — enforce via depends_on, not prose. The map names, per deleted block, a concrete emitter + OVERSEER_ALERT subject + the SKILL.md surface that renders it. Any block mapping to NO emitter is a HITL raised at the point of discovery.
risks.review_gate: task_planner encodes D1 → {D2,D3} depends_on edges; reviewer_plan confirms the gate is a real verification task with a HITL escape, not a rubber stamp.

risks.risk: Over-deletion removes the render-on-OVERSEER_ALERT AskUserQuestion flows (Long-Running Implement Phase + Unresolved NACK) while stripping host-side detection prose (AC-D3). Highest-consequence regression in PR D — the skill would stop surfacing alerts it still receives.
risks.mitigation: Scope the deletion to detection/trigger prose ONLY. Preserve both render-on-alert flows, the user-initiated Stuck Pipeline Rescue workflow (Steps 1-3 minus its host-side detection trigger), and the two thin last-resort backstops.
risks.review_gate: Reviewer criterion: both render-on-alert AskUserQuestion flows still fire on their OVERSEER_ALERTs post-deletion; Rescue workflow + backstops intact.

risks.risk: overseer_owns_host_detection removal is incomplete — a dangling getattr/reference or config key remains, leaving dead-but-live code that silently reads a now-absent field.
risks.mitigation: Remove the Field (_config.py:388) AND both getattr refs (_routes_status.py:126-127); grep-clean of the symbol is the completion check (grounded: only these two production refs exist).
risks.review_gate: grep for 'overseer_owns_host_detection' returns empty across the tree.

risks.risk: Soft merge seam: PR B edits orchestrator/routes/pipelines/__init__.py (allowlist) and PR D edits _routes_status.py (:126-127) — same split package. Concurrent landing could conflict or produce a subtle interaction in the /status/wait path.
risks.mitigation: Different regions of the package; flag for reviewer merge-seam awareness. No cross-blocking depends_on edge needed, but note it in the slice DAG so reviewers watch it if B and D land close together.
risks.review_gate: Reviewer notes the shared package; confirm the two edits do not overlap on landing.

risks.risk: The host agent-* vocab (agent-stall / agent-silent / agent-nack-unresolved / phase-long-running) has NO deterministic overseer emitter — it exists in production only as a last-alert dedup map (shared/egg_overseer/state.py:86) and is otherwise produced by the overseer Haiku classifier (LLM path). So 'parity' for those blocks rests on a probabilistic classifier firing, not a structural threshold detector.
risks.mitigation: The coverage-map must distinguish structural _broadcast_alert emitters (post_consensus_stall, incomplete_consensus_stall, etc.) from the classifier path, and for classifier-only blocks state explicitly that parity = 'the overseer classifies and emits an OVERSEER_ALERT the skill surfaces'. Any block whose parity cannot be confirmed on EITHER path is a HITL, not a delete.
risks.review_gate: Coverage-map labels each block's emitter path (structural vs classifier); classifier-only blocks are called out, not silently assumed equivalent to a deterministic detector.

cross_cutting.note: cq-1 is BINDING (human-resolved opt-3): PR C must implement unbounded paced retry + a threshold OVERSEER_ALERT and MUST NOT introduce any hard wall-clock ceiling/halt. Reviewer_plan and the eventual coder must both hold this line (RC5).

Slice DAG: B, C, D are independent with NO cross-blocking edges. The ONLY ordering constraint is PR D's internal gate — D1 (coverage-map) blocks D2 (SKILL.md deletion) and D3 (flag removal). This must be encoded as task-level depends_on, not left to prose (RD1).

Test-coverage weighting: PR C (RC1-RC4, RC8-RC9) carries the heaviest behavioral risk and should receive the densest test coverage; PR B is additive with two sharp edges (lock + allowlist); PR D risk is concentrated in the gate (RD1) and render-on-alert preservation (RD2).

cq-2 is BINDING (human-resolved opt-3, resolved during implement 2026-07-06T23:47Z): PR C was PAUSED and sent back for re-plan/re-scope because its 3-file scope is unfaithful — the throttle signature is not observable as text at the recording layer (RC8) and JobSupervisor relocated to event_loop/ (#3447, RC9). This plan round MUST reconcile PR C's file set with the exit-code mechanism and the post-#3447 anchors before implement resumes. A re-proposed PR C that repeats the stale 3-file/error-text-at-streak-site design is a NACK. PR B and PR D were NOT paused by cq-2 and their assessments are unchanged.

nack_conditions: PR C re-plan does not reconcile the file set per cq-2: it keeps the stale 3-file scope and the falsified 'throttle wording observable at the streak site' premise instead of the exit-code mechanism (new EX_RATE_LIMITED mirroring EX_AUTH_FATAL through auth_errors → __main__ → kubernetes_spawner → event_loop/_loop → event_loop/_supervisor), and does NOT explicitly document the cq-2 opt-2 partial-AC-C1 deviation the operator declined (RC8).

PR C plan retains stale post-#3447 anchors (concurrent_executor.py:988 as the streak site, or 'JobSupervisor in concurrent_executor.py') instead of re-grounding to event_loop/_supervisor.py + _handle_arms_exhausted:1076 (RC9).
PR C classification is derived from error TEXT at the orchestrator/recording layer (which never receives it) rather than from a distinct exit code decided at the agent CLI (RC8/RC1).
PR C introduces a hard wall-clock ceiling/halt, contradicting cq-1 (RC5), or lacks a deterministic-loop guard as the structural stop (RC2).
PR C plan does not require a landed-slice-preservation test for the restart_phase-equivalent (RC4), or lacks an AC-C6 invariance regression across the NEW exit-code plumbing (RC9).
PR D does not encode D1 (coverage-map) as a task-level blocker on D2/D3 (RD1), or treats the coverage-map as a rubber stamp with no HITL escape for unmapped blocks.
PR D deletion task is not scoped to detection/trigger prose only, or lacks a reviewer criterion that both render-on-alert flows still fire (RD2).
PR B emits slice.closed inside the scheduler lock (RB1) or omits the _STATUS_WAIT_EVENT_TYPES allowlist entry + its test (RB2).
